subject: VitalArc technical qualification & Redwood eval runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Amira Shah <amira.shah@vitalarc.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@vitalarc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: VitalArc technical qualification & Redwood eval runbook

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a realistic model-fit readout within 7 business days.

What we heard (short):
- Goal: extract structured disposition and intent from inbound clinical intake notes (high precision on entity spans + conservative hallucination profile).
- Volume: ~250k notes/year; for initial eval you can share ~1,200 de-identified rows.
- Success signals: entity F1 >= 0.78 on core fields (diagnosis_code, medication_name) and <2% critical hallucination rate on a 300-sample adjudication.

Redwood proposal (next steps):
1) You drop a 1,200-row sample CSV (format below). We’ll run three candidate models with the same prompt sets and scoring script.
2) Turnaround: baseline run in 3 business days + sanity review, full scoring within 7 business days.
3) Deliverable: model comparison (precision/recall/F1 per field), hallucination audit, latency/cost estimate per 1k tokens, and recommended configuration (quantization/batching settings).

Recommended candidate models (to cover cost/quality spectrum):
- Mistral-instruct-7B (fast, lower cost)
- Llama-2-13b-chat (balanced)
- Redwood-7B-optimized (our tuned variant for clinical extraction; better prefix caching)

Dataset format (please use the sample we attached):
- CSV columns: id, note_text, gold_entities_json (list of spans + labels), source_date
- De-identify PHI before upload. We can accept a token flagging column if you want to retain linkage.

Attachments: vitalarc_eval_dataset_sample.csv (format stub), vitalarc_prompt_sets_v1.md, vitalarc_scoring_guide_v1.md

Links: drive folder with runbook and scoring notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEf-VitalArc-eval-repo

Asks for you:
- Confirm we can run on the sample and that the dataset is fully de-identified.
- Who should receive the final report? I’ll include Amira + Tom + your security contact if you want SOC2 language in the artifact.

If this looks good I’ll kick off the run once you upload the CSV to the Drive folder and confirm permission.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Amira Shah <amira.shah@vitalarc.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VitalArc technical qualification & Redwood eval runbook

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming: we can provide a 1,200-row de-identified export by EOD Monday. A couple of clarifications before you run: 

1) Gold labels: our team exported entity spans in a custom JSON — should we convert to the simple span+label CSV or leave as JSON in the gold_entities_json column?
2) Sensitive fields: there are rare PHI tokens (provider initials) that we can token-mask; will that affect hallucination checks?
3) Security: please share the minimum retention window for the trial artifacts and whether Redwood will purge all eval outputs on request.

We’d like the final report to go to me and Tom; I’ll loop in our security engineering contact separately if needed.

—Amira
Amira Shah | Head of Data Science, VitalArc
amira.shah@vitalarc.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: VitalArc technical qualification & Redwood eval runbook

Looping you in — VitalArc will upload a 1,200-row sample Monday EOD. They asked three operational/security clarifications: gold label format, PHI token masking impact, and retention/purge policy.

Operational asks for the eval team (Karthik / Laura):
- Confirm the scoring script accepts gold_entities_json as a single JSON-encoded column (we can parse on our side). If not, provide the conversion step.
- Recommend default quantization/instance type to run the three candidates at scale (cost estimate).
- Draft the retention statement and purge SLA we can send to Amira (they want to know we’ll purge trial outputs on request).

Karthik — can you take the scoring/format check? Laura — can you draft a one-paragraph retention/purge note (legal-friendly) we can send to VitalArc? I’ll sync with Ben on timeline.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Cc: Amira Shah <amira.shah@vitalarc.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VitalArc technical qualification & Redwood eval runbook

Thanks — quick answers and proposed config we can send to Amira: 

1) Format: we can accept gold_entities_json as a JSON-encoded cell. Our scoring pipeline will parse lists of {start,end,label}. We’ll include a small conversion notebook in the Drive folder for edge cases.

2) PHI masking: token-masked provider initials are fine. Hallucination checks work the same — we flag outputs that contain tokens not present in the input and run a second-stage fuzzy-match across gold spans to catch label hallucination. Note: masking may slightly reduce entity span recall where the model relied on provider context; we’ll call this out in the report.

3) Retention/purge: proposed wording — "Redwood Inference will retain trial artifacts (raw model outputs, logs, and scoring metadata) for 30 days following delivery of the eval report. On request, Redwood will securely purge all trial artifacts within 48 hours and provide confirmation of deletion." Please run this by legal if you need a different window.

Run config (initial):
- Mistral-instruct-7B: 1x g5.2xlarge-equivalent with q4-opts, batching 16
- Llama-2-13b-chat: 2x g5.4xlarge-equivalent with fp16, batching 8
- Redwood-7B-optimized: 1x g5.2xlarge-equivalent with q4-opts and prefix caching enabled
Estimated baseline cost: $1,200 for full 3-model run on 1,200 rows (includes scoring). We’ll provide exact token counts after we ingest the sample.

I’ll add the conversion notebook and a short scoring README to the Drive folder now. Marissa/Ben — if this is ok I’ll go ahead once Amira confirms upload.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Inferencing Engineer, Redwood Inference
